title: Now in Makkah: The Islam of Hamzah (RA) • Allah Sometimes Straightens Even Along a Crooked Path • The Day ‘Umar (RA) Went Out Sword in Hand • The Man Who Changed on a Single Page • After the Islam of ‘Umar • What a Single Page Can Do • Others Who Came • Final Word

blocks.0: Now in Makkah: The Islam of Hamzah (RA)
blocks.1: Leaving the news of Abyssinia here, let us return to Makkah. In Makkah the persecution was still going on. In the midst of it two events occurred that changed the whole reckoning. One day Abu Jahl found the Prophet {{1}} alone near the mount of Safa, said all sorts of things, and raised a hand against him. The Prophet {{2}} said not a word. He came away.
blocks.2: Nearby, a slave-woman of ‘Abdullah ibn Jud‘an stood and saw it all. That afternoon Hamzah (RA) returned from hunting, bow on his shoulder. He was one of the bravest men of Makkah, the uncle of the Prophet {{1}}, and his milk-brother.
blocks.3: The custom of Makkah was that on returning from hunting he would first circle the Ka‘bah. That day on the way the slave-woman stopped him and told him everything; how Abu Jahl had humiliated your nephew today, and he did not say a word.
blocks.4: Hamzah’s (RA) blood boiled. He went straight to the Ka‘bah, found Abu Jahl, and split his head with the bow. He said, you abuse my nephew! I too am on his din. If you can, settle it with me.{{1}}
blocks.5: Abu Jahl fell silent. When his men rose to their feet he stopped them; he said, leave it, I really did speak ill of his nephew. At first this was tribal stubbornness; why should anyone touch my man.
blocks.6: Allah Sometimes Straightens Even Along a Crooked Path
blocks.7: Hamzah (RA) came home. Back home a doubt struck him. I have said it with my mouth, I am on the din of Muhammad. But have I truly accepted it inside! Or did I say it in a fit of anger!
blocks.8: He remained restless all night. In the end he raised his hands to Allah, make my heart steady; let me stay on this path knowingly and understandingly. After that Allah opened his chest. The stubbornness took the form of faith.{{1}}
blocks.9: There is something to think about in this incident. The first step of Hamzah (RA) was not entirely with the right intention. Anger, tribal pride, the insult to the nephew; this was the pull. Yet the word that came out of the mouth from that anger was a true word. And Allah took hold of that truth and lifted him up.
blocks.10: We often tell ourselves, the intention is not right, so I do not even begin the deed. Yet often when the deed begins the intention is set right afterward. I began going to the mosque out of shame before people; later I went out of love. I took up the Qur’an for fear of the exam; later I found peace in the recitation itself.
blocks.11: When the intention is not right, a good deed should not be left aside. One holds on to the deed and mends the intention. Hamzah (RA), on returning home, did exactly this; he made du‘a and set his heart straight.
blocks.12: The Day ‘Umar (RA) Went Out Sword in Hand
blocks.13: This is a few days after the Islam of Hamzah (RA). ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab was then one of the fiercest enemies of Islam. A strong hand, a harsh temper, known as the envoy of Makkah.
blocks.14: One day he went out with a sword in hand. One intention only; today he would finish Muhammad. On the way he met Nu‘aym ibn ‘Abdillah; he had become a Muslim in secret. He asked, where are you going, ‘Umar. ‘Umar said, to Muhammad. To finish him.
blocks.15: Nu‘aym said, first set your own house in order. Your sister Fatimah and brother-in-law Sa‘id have taken that din. ‘Umar turned around. Now the target was his sister’s house. Nearing the house he heard someone inside reciting something in a low voice. Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) was teaching them Surah Ta-Ha.
blocks.16: ‘Umar pushed the door and entered. He seized his brother-in-law Sa‘id and beat him. When his sister Fatimah tried to shield him, she was struck in the face too, and blood came out. With a blood-stained face Fatimah (RA) said, ‘Umar, do what you like. But we will not give up this din.{{1}}
blocks.17: His sister’s blood, and this word of his sister; the two together stopped ‘Umar. The anger inside him suddenly softened. He said, show me once what you were reading.
blocks.18: The Man Who Changed on a Single Page
blocks.19: Fatimah (RA) said, you are impure. Bathe before touching this writing. The hardest man of Makkah, hearing his sister’s word, bathed. Then he took the sheet in his hand.
blocks.20: On it was written the beginning of Surah Ta-Ha
blocks.22: Ta-Ha. I have not sent down this Qur’an to you that you should suffer. Rather it is an admonition for one who fears. It is a revelation from Him who created the earth and the lofty heavens. The Most Merciful is established above the Throne. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath the soil.{{1}}
blocks.23: ‘Umar stopped as he read. He said, how beautiful is this word, how dignified. Khabbab (RA) had been hiding inside the house all this time. Coming out he said, ‘Umar, by Allah, I hope He has chosen you. Only yesterday I heard the Prophet {{1}} say, O Allah, strengthen Islam with ‘Umar or Abu Jahl.{{2}}
blocks.24: ‘Umar asked, where is Muhammad now. Khabbab (RA) said, near Safa, in Dar al-Arqam. ‘Umar went to Dar al-Arqam with that same sword in hand. He knocked at the door. The Companions were afraid; ‘Umar standing with a sword. Hamzah (RA) said, let him in. If he has come with a good intention, good; if with a bad intention, his matter will be settled with his own sword.
blocks.25: ‘Umar went inside and said, I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah, and you are the Messenger of Allah. Dar al-Arqam shook with the takbir. The people of Makkah heard that sound outside.
blocks.26: A man had left home to kill. After reading a single page of the Qur’an, he went back a Muslim.
blocks.28: ‘Umar (RA) was not one to accept Islam and stay quiet. He asked the Prophet {{1}}, are we not on the truth, whether we die or live! The Prophet {{2}} said, certainly. ‘Umar said, then why hide. Come, openly.
blocks.29: Until then the Companions did not dare to pray openly in front of the Ka‘bah. On the day of ‘Umar’s Islam that changed. That day the Companions went toward the Ka‘bah in two rows. At the head of one row Hamzah (RA), at the head of the other ‘Umar (RA).
blocks.30: The Quraysh stared, and could do nothing. That day the Muslims for the first time prayed openly, with open eyes, in front of the Ka‘bah. ‘Umar (RA) himself went and told the assembly of the Quraysh, I have become a Muslim. They flared up in anger, but no one had the courage to say anything to his face.
blocks.31: ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) would say later, since the Islam of ‘Umar we have prayed with honour.{{1}}
blocks.32: One man’s inside changed. And on the strength of his courage the whole community stood with head raised. Sometimes one person’s firmness breaks the fear of a whole group. In a gathering, if one person dares to say the right thing, the others too find the strength to speak.
blocks.33: What a Single Page Can Do
blocks.34: What is the biggest point in the story of ‘Umar (RA)! Not the sword. Not the sister’s courage. Not even the Islam of Hamzah (RA). The biggest point: a man had set out to kill, and after reading one page of the Qur’an he went back a Muslim.
blocks.35: Within the Qur’an is a power that people do not want to open and see for themselves. ‘Umar had been told since childhood, this is poetry, this is magic, this is the raving of a madman. All this time without verifying himself he had believed those words. The moment he put his own eyes on it, all those notions fell apart on a single page.
blocks.36: We too hear many things and do not verify. The Qur’an is hard, I will not understand; reciting is enough, meaning is not needed; that is the work of scholars. We recite a lot. We pause little.
blocks.37: To stop before a verse and think, is this really being said to me; this is what stopped ‘Umar. The Qur’an that could change a man like ‘Umar in one sitting, that same Qur’an lies open before me every day.
blocks.38: The question is not about the power of the Qur’an. The question is whether I am sitting before it, pausing, with attention.
blocks.40: In this period a few more people came to Islam; each by a different path. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) had come earlier, stood before the Ka‘bah and testified openly and was beaten; that came in the last dars.{{1}}
blocks.41: Tufayl ibn ‘Amr al-Dawsi was a chief of a tribe and a well-known poet. Before he entered Makkah the Quraysh surrounded him; do not listen to Muhammad’s words, there is magic in his words; you and your tribe will be ruined.
blocks.42: He was so afraid that he went to the Ka‘bah with cotton stuffed in his ears, so that by mistake no word of the Prophet {{1}} would enter his ear. Yet a few words got into his ears. He thought, I am an intelligent man, a poet, I can tell good from bad. What is the use of cotton in my ears; let me listen once, if it is good I will take it, if bad I will leave it.
blocks.44: Dimad al-Azdi used to practise incantation-healing; treating jinn and wind. Coming to Makkah he heard people say Muhammad is mad. He thought, let me try, perhaps Allah will cure him at my hands.
blocks.45: Going to the Prophet {{1}} he said, let me hear your words once. The Prophet {{2}} spoke some words beginning with the praise of Allah. Dimad said, repeat these words to me. Then he said, I have heard the words of soothsayers, I have heard the words of sorcerers, I have heard the words of poets; such words I have heard from no one’s mouth. Take my pledge.{{3}}
blocks.46: Three people. They came in through three different doors. One from anger, one from curiosity, one with a wrong notion. One thing alone drew them all. Once the word had reached the ear, it could not be denied.
blocks.48: In today’s dars we saw what happened when persecution reached everyone. A group of Companions crossed the sea to Abyssinia to save the din. There the Qur’an reached a royal court, a Christian king wept, and in the end came as far as faith.
blocks.49: And in Makkah two men; Hamzah and ‘Umar (RA); came and stood by two different paths. Then the Muslims for the first time prayed with heads held high before the Ka‘bah. One thing came up again and again through the whole dars. One recitation overturned the king’s decision. One page of the Qur’an changed ‘Umar. A few words stopped Tufayl and Dimad.
blocks.50: That power of the Qur’an has not diminished even a little today. One more thing. Ja‘far (RA) did not give a long speech in the king’s court. He said two things; what we were before, and what he came and changed.
blocks.51: If someone suddenly asks today, what does your din actually teach; do I have an ordered answer like Ja‘far’s! Or do I glance about and turn the conversation?
blocks.52: So take one task from today’s dars. In your own words, in two or three lines, put in order an introduction to Islam. What people were like before, and what this din came and changed.
blocks.53: So that when someone asks you need not freeze. In the coming dars we shall see what the Quraysh did after these two accepted Islam; the whole of Banu Hashim was besieged in a valley for three years.
blocks.55: Ja‘far (RA), standing in the court of the emperor, said in two minutes what we were before and what this din came and changed. Today I will ask myself one question: if someone asks what my din teaches, will I be able to say it in order?
blocks.56: Today I will write a two-or-three-line introduction in my own words and memorise it, which from today I will no longer leave disordered.

footnotes.0: Concerning the humiliation of the Prophet {{1}} at the hands of Abu Jahl, the witness of the slave-woman of ‘Abdullah ibn Jud‘an, and Hamzah (RA) splitting Abu Jahl’s head with his bow and declaring Islam: Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham. The narration is of the Sirah works; the chain is mursal. That Hamzah (RA) accepted Islam in the earliest period and was later martyred at Uhud is established by sound chains.
footnotes.1: Concerning the doubt in the heart after Hamzah’s (RA) declaration of Islam, returning home, and gaining firmness by praying to Allah to steady the heart: Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham. The narration is of the Sirah works; the chain is mursal.
footnotes.2: Concerning ‘Umar (RA) going out sword in hand, meeting Nu‘aym, the sheet of Surah Ta-Ha in the house of his sister Fatimah and brother-in-law Sa‘id ibn Zayd (RA), and accepting Islam from there: Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham; al-Daraqutni; Ibn Sa‘d. The chain of the full incident is mursal and has some weakness. But the Islam of ‘Umar (RA) and its effect are established by sound chains.
footnotes.4: The du‘a of the Prophet {{1}}, ‘O Allah, strengthen Islam with ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab or Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, whichever of the two is dearer to You’, and ‘Umar’s (RA) acceptance of Islam the next day: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi, hadith 3681; Musnad Ahmad; Ibn Majah, hadith 105. Many hadith scholars have called the narration hasan.
footnotes.5: ‘Ma zilna a‘izzatan mundhu aslama ‘Umar’; since ‘Umar’s Islam we have been honoured. Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3684; via ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA). ✓ Verified. This is Ibn Mas‘ud’s (RA) own statement; sahih by the standard of Imam al-Bukhari.
footnotes.6: Details of the acceptance of Islam by Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) and his open testimony of the kalimah in al-Masjid al-Haram: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3522; Sahih Muslim, hadith 2474. Given in detail in Dars 7.
footnotes.7: Concerning Tufayl ibn ‘Amr al-Dawsi (RA) going to the Ka‘bah with cotton in his ears and later accepting Islam: Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham. The narration is of the Sirah works; the chain is mursal.
footnotes.8: The incident of the acceptance of Islam by Dimad al-Azdi (RA): Sahih Muslim, hadith 868; via Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). ✓ Verified.

quiz.q: Who brought the news of Abu Jahl’s insult to Hamzah (RA)?
o: The Prophet ﷺ himself told him
quiz.e: The slave-woman had seen everything near the mount of Safa; she told Hamzah (RA), returning from the hunt.

quiz.q: With what did Hamzah (RA) split Abu Jahl’s head?
quiz.e: He had a bow on his shoulder returning from hunting; with it he went to the Ka‘bah and declared Islam.

quiz.q: What was the difference between Hamzah’s (RA) first step and his final faith?
o: Actually there was no difference between the two
First stubbornness, later steadiness of heart through du‘a
First firm faith, later doubt in the mind
quiz.e: Back home a doubt struck him; he prayed to steady his heart, and the stubbornness took the form of faith.

quiz.q: What example does the dars give in support of ‘if the intention is not right, a deed should not be left’?
o: The martyrdom of Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA)
Going to the mosque out of shame before people and later going out of love
quiz.e: If one holds on to the deed the intention can be mended later; Hamzah (RA) did exactly this on returning home.

quiz.q: What is the advice about a good deed when the intention is not fully right?
o: Wait until the intention is right
Leave the deed aside for now
Do it only after informing people
Hold on to the deed and mend the intention
quiz.e: Going to the mosque began out of shame before people, later out of love; Hamzah (RA) prayed and straightened his heart.

quiz.q: Who turned ‘Umar (RA) toward his sister’s house?
quiz.e: Nu‘aym told ‘Umar, who had set out sword in hand, first set your own house in order; your sister and brother-in-law have taken that din.

quiz.q: Who was teaching Surah Ta-Ha in ‘Umar’s sister’s house?
quiz.e: When ‘Umar entered, Khabbab (RA) hid; later he came out and spoke of the du‘a of the Prophet ﷺ.

quiz.q: What did Fatimah (RA) tell ‘Umar to do before touching the sheet?
quiz.e: Saying you are impure she had him bathe first; then ‘Umar took the sheet in his hand.

quiz.q: Strengthening Islam through one of which two did the Prophet ﷺ pray for?
quiz.e: ‘O Allah, ‘Umar or Abu Jahl; strengthen Islam with the one dearer to You’; Tirmidhi 3681.

quiz.q: Who said to let ‘Umar in on seeing him with a sword in Dar al-Arqam?
quiz.e: Hamzah (RA) said, let him in; if with good intention, good, otherwise his matter will be settled with his own sword.

quiz.q: What were the Companions able to do for the first time after ‘Umar’s (RA) Islam?
o: Secretly send envoys to the tribes of Madinah
Make a written treaty with the Quraysh
Migrate to Abyssinia in a group
quiz.e: In two rows, Hamzah and ‘Umar (RA) at the front; the Quraysh stared and could do nothing.

quiz.q: Who says, ‘since the Islam of ‘Umar we have prayed with honour’?
quiz.e: ‘Ma zilna a‘izzatan mundhu aslama ‘Umar’; Sahih al-Bukhari 3684, the statement of Ibn Mas‘ud (RA).

quiz.q: How does one person’s firmness change a whole group, from the story of ‘Umar?
o: By his becoming leader of the whole group
By his giving away his wealth
By his openly declaring war before everyone
Through his courage the rest gain strength to stand
quiz.e: ‘Umar, on accepting Islam, spoke of open prayer; from then the Companions prayed with heads raised.

quiz.q: In the story of ‘Umar’s Islam, what is the biggest point according to the dars?
o: The sister’s courage with a blood-stained face
Changing on reading one page of the Qur’an
quiz.e: That power of the Qur’an which people do not want to open and see for themselves; ‘Umar changed because he paused and thought.

quiz.q: ‘The question is not about the power of the Qur’an, but whether I am sitting before it’; what does this mean?
o: To be affected, one must sit and pay attention
The Qur’an is really not for all people
If one does not understand the meaning, recitation is of no benefit
quiz.e: We recite a lot, we pause little; one thought alone stopped ‘Umar.

quiz.q: Which habit does the dars name for benefiting from the Qur’an?
o: Pausing and thinking at one verse
quiz.e: ‘Is this being said to me?’; this thought is what stopped ‘Umar (RA).

quiz.q: What did Tufayl ibn ‘Amr do on going to the Ka‘bah out of fear of the Quraysh?
o: Covered his whole face with cloth
Kept both eyes closed the whole time
Took a few companions with him
quiz.e: The Quraysh had said there is magic in Muhammad’s words; yet when a few words got into his ears he decided to listen once.

quiz.q: What work did Dimad al-Azdi do?
quiz.e: Hearing ‘mad’ he went to cure him; hearing the words of the Prophet ﷺ he said, these are not the words of any madman. Sahih Muslim 868.

quiz.q: In the part ‘Others Who Came’, what is the common point in the Islam of the three?
o: All three were great tribal chiefs
Once the word reached the ear they could not deny it
All three had been severely persecuted
quiz.e: One from anger, one from curiosity, one with a wrong notion; one thing alone drew them all.

quiz.q: What lesson does the part ‘Others Who Came’ give about da‘wah?
o: Getting the word to the ear is the real work
Everyone should be called in the same way
Only the intelligent should be called
Calling fierce opponents is utterly futile
quiz.e: Coming from anger, curiosity or a wrong notion they could not stay away; once the word reaches the ear denial is hard.

quiz.q: If someone asks ‘what does your din teach’, what is the preparation?
quiz.e: Ja‘far said in two minutes what we were before and what he came and changed; today’s practical resolve is this too.

quiz.q: What is the practical resolve of this dars?
o: Keep an ordered introduction to the din in one’s own words
Read a large book of the Sirah
Invite at least one person a week
quiz.e: What people were like before, and what this din came and changed; so that when someone asks one need not freeze.
